**Bottom line: all three have now taken oath as Supreme Court judges. On current information the question resolves as 3.**

**Timeline**
- **28 Sep 2026:** The Supreme Court Collegium recommended all three for elevation. The Collegium is headed by CJI Surya Kant.
- **5 Oct 2026 (Monday):** The Department of Justice notified all three appointments through a notification dated 5 October 2026. The appointments take effect from the date each judge assumes charge.
- **6 Oct 2026 (Tuesday, today):** CJI Surya Kant swore in all three at a 3.30 pm ceremony, which the Court live-streamed on its YouTube channel. Swearings-in are normally at 10.30 am, so the afternoon timing was unusual, but it doesn't affect the question. IANS, ANI, PTI/ETV Bharat and the Tribune all report the oaths.
- The Court's working strength is now 37, including the CJI, against a sanctioned strength of 38. Agarwal's elevation brings the number of sitting women judges to three.

**Resolution sources**
- **sci.gov.in "Chief Justice & Judges" page:** My search didn't return this page, so I can't confirm it lists them yet. The Court usually updates the list within days of an oath. If the page is slow or down, the fallback clause accepts credible reporting of the oaths, and that reporting now exists.
- **Metaculus FAQ ("credible sources"):** Not retrieved. The outlets reporting the oaths (ANI, IANS, PTI, Tribune, Bar & Bench, SCC Online) would plainly count.

**What could still change the outcome before 17 Oct**
- **Retirement:** None of the three is close to the retirement age of 65. Upadhyaya was born 16 June 1965 and Singh 7 July 1965, so both are 61. Agarwal will retire from the Court in April 2031.
- **Other exits:** Death, resignation or removal within 11 days would be extremely unlikely. Removal requires impeachment by Parliament, and nothing of that kind is pending.
- **Remaining risk:** Mostly technical, such as the official page not being updated by 17 Oct. Even then, the fallback clause would cover it.

**Base rate:** Supreme Court judges almost never leave office within weeks of taking oath.

**Scheduled events:** None that bear on this question before 17 Oct.

**Prediction markets:** I didn't find any.

**Sources:**

- [2](https://www.scconline.com/blog/post/2026/10/06/president-appoints-3-high-court-chief-justices-as-supreme-court-judges/)
- [3](https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/india/cji-surya-kant-administers-oath-of-office-to-three-newly-appointed-supreme-court-judges)

criterios: This question resolves as the number (0, 1, 2, or 3) of the following three persons who appear as sitting judges on the Supreme Court of India's official "Chief Justice & Judges" list at https://www.sci.gov.in/chief-justice-judges/ as of October 17, 2026: (1) Justice Sunita Agarwal, (2) Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya, and (3) Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh. A person counts only if their name appears on that list as a sitting Supreme Court judge (i.e., they have been appointed and taken oath), regardless of their listed date of appointment. For example, if two of the three appear on the list and one does not, this resolves as 2.
letra_pequena: If the official Supreme Court of India page is unavailable, resolution will rely on equivalent official notifications or reporting by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) confirming whether each named person has been sworn in as a Supreme Court of India judge on or before October 17, 2026. These three persons were recommended for elevation by the Supreme Court Collegium on 28 September 2026 while serving as High Court Chief Justices (Agarwal: Gujarat; Upadhyaya: Delhi; Singh: Telangana); the count is based solely on whether each has taken oath as a Supreme Court judge by the resolution date.

(c) **If the current trend continued:** 3. Once sworn in, judges stay on the Court. None of the three is near the retirement age of 65.

(d) **Experts and markets:** Credible media unanimously report all three oaths. No prediction markets were found.

(e) **Unexpected low scenario:** The reports are mistaken, or the official page is stale and the resolver doesn't apply the fallback clause. A judge could also die or resign within days. All of these are very unlikely.

(f) **Unexpected high scenario:** 3 is already the maximum possible.
